query_database.py:122 sets fence length to max(3, 1+longest backtick run in sql). Under CommonMark, which the standard markdown-it fence rule implements, a closing fence needs at least as many fence characters as the opener. Every backtick-only line in the SQL is no longer than the longest run, so it is shorter than the opener and cannot close the block. The info string 'sql' has no backticks, so the opener is valid. The text is preceded by a blank line (line 123), so it starts a new top-level block. The renderer (query_results.html:776-791) uses markdownit with html false and only disables images, so the fence rule is not altered. I did not read the vendored markdown-it.min.js bytes and did not execute the renderer. This rests on the standard CommonMark fence algorithm.
